tools.name: content-management
tools.description:
<use_case>
      Unified tool for all content management operations including publishing, previewing, 
      code deployment, and cache management. Use the 'operation' parameter to specify 
      the desired action.

      **Available Operations:**
      - publish-status: Get publish status of a resource
      - publish-resource: Publish a resource to make it live
      - unpublish-resource: Remove a resource from live site
      - bulk-publish: Start bulk publish job
      - preview-status: Get preview status of a resource
      - update-preview: Update preview for a resource
      - delete-preview: Delete preview version of a resource
      - bulk-preview: Start bulk preview job
      - code-status: Get code deployment status
      - update-code: Deploy code for a resource
      - delete-code: Remove code deployment
      - batch-update-code: Batch code update
      - purge-cache: Purge live cache for a resource
    </use_case>

    <important_notes>
      1. Most operations require org, site, and path parameters
      2. Some operations may be destructive (publish, delete, purge)
      3. Bulk operations return job IDs for tracking
      4. Cache operations may take time to propagate globally
    </important_notes>

operation.description: The content management operation to perform

tools.name: organization-config
tools.description:
<use_case>
      Tool for managing organization-level configuration settings.
      Use the 'operation' parameter to specify the desired action.

      **Available Operations:**
      - get-org-config: Get organization configuration
      - update-org-config: Update organization configuration
    </use_case>

    <important_notes>
      1. Organization configuration operations may require admin permissions
      2. Changes affect all sites in the organization
      3. Configuration changes may require system restart or cache refresh
      4. Update operations are destructive and affect live systems
    </important_notes>

operation.description: The organization configuration operation to perform

tools.name: site-config
tools.description:
<use_case>
      Tool for managing site-level configuration settings including site, 
      index, and sitemap configurations. Use the 'operation' parameter to 
      specify the desired action.

      **Available Operations:**
      - get-site-config: Get site configuration
      - update-site-config: Update site configuration
      - get-index-config: Get index configuration for a site
      - update-index-config: Update index configuration for a site
      - get-sitemap-config: Get sitemap configuration for a site
      - update-sitemap-config: Update sitemap configuration for a site
    </use_case>

    <important_notes>
      1. Site configuration operations may require admin permissions
      2. Changes affect site functionality and should be tested
      3. Some configurations may require re-indexing or regeneration
      4. Update operations are destructive and affect live systems
    </important_notes>

operation.description: The site configuration operation to perform

tools.name: job-browser
tools.description: Read-only access to list jobs and inspect job status/details.

tools.name: authentication
tools.description:
<use_case>
      Unified tool for managing authentication operations including login selection,
      automatic login, logout, and profile information. Use the 'operation' parameter
      to specify the desired action.

      **Available Operations:**
      - login-selection: Get available login options and authentication methods
      - auto-login: Attempt automatic login using stored credentials or tokens
      - logout: Logout from current session and invalidate tokens
      - profile-info: Get profile information for currently authenticated user
    </use_case>

    <important_notes>
      1. Authentication operations affect user sessions and access
      2. Logout operations invalidate all active sessions
      3. Profile operations require valid authentication
      4. Auto-login may fail if tokens are expired
    </important_notes>

tools.name: search-operations
tools.description:
<use_case>
      Unified tool for search and indexing operations including index status,
      re-indexing resources, removing from index, and sitemap generation.
      Use the 'operation' parameter to specify the desired action.

      **Available Operations:**
      - index-status: Get the index status of a specific resource
      - reindex-resource: Re-index a specific resource to update search index
      - remove-from-index: Remove a specific resource from search index
      - generate-sitemap: Generate sitemap for the site
    </use_case>

    <important_notes>
      1. Index operations affect searchability of content
      2. Re-indexing may take time to process and propagate
      3. Sitemap generation may take time for large sites
      4. Resources must be published to be indexed
    </important_notes>

tools.name: page-status
tools.description:
<use_case>
      Use this tool to retrieve the status of a single page. The results will include information for when the page
      was last published, previewed, and edited, as well as who performed those actions.
      
      **When to use this tool:**
      - You need status information for ONE specific page
      - You know the exact page path
      - You want immediate results (synchronous)
      - You're checking if a specific page is published/previewed
      - You need to verify when a page was last updated
    </use_case>

    <important_notes>
      1. The org, site, branch, and path must be provided, ask the user for them if they are not provided.
      2. The org, site, branch, and path can be derived from the aem page URL. This is of the form: https://${branch}--${site}--${org}.aem.live/${path}
      3. Do not make up any information, only use the information that is provided in the response to answer the user's question.
    </important_notes>

tools.name: bulk-status
tools.description: Start or check asynchronous bulk page-status jobs

tools.name: audit-log
tools.description:
<use_case>
      Use this tool to retrieve audit logs from the AEM Edge Delivery Services repository. The results will include detailed information about 
      repository activities and operations. The response contains a list of entries with the following information:
      
      - **timestamp**: Unix timestamp when the action occurred
      - **user**: Email address of the user who performed the action
      - **route**: Type of operation (e.g., "preview", "live", "job")
      - **method**: HTTP method used (e.g., "POST", "GET")
      - **path**: The specific resource path that was affected
      - **status**: HTTP status code of the operation result (e.g., 200, 404, 500)
      - **duration**: Time taken for the operation in milliseconds
      - **contentBusId**: Unique identifier for the content being processed
      - **org/site/repo/ref**: Repository and branch information
      - **job**: Job identifier (for job-related operations)
      
      Common route types include:
      - "preview": Content preview operations
      - "live": Live content publishing operations  
      - "job": Background job operations (publish, index, etc.)
      
      The response also includes "from" and "to" timestamps indicating the time range of the logs.
      
      **When to use this tool:**
      - You need to investigate system errors or failures
      - You want to see who performed specific actions and when
      - You're troubleshooting publishing or preview issues
      - You need to audit user activity and system operations
      - You want to monitor system performance (duration times)
      - You're debugging deployment or publishing problems
      - You need to track content changes over time
      - You want to verify if specific operations completed successfully
      - You're investigating slow performance or timeouts
      - You need to see the sequence of operations that occurred
      - You want to see if something was published or previewed
      
      **When NOT to use this tool:**
      - You need current page status information (use page-status or bulk-status tools)
      - You want to check if a page is published/previewed
      - You need to find pages with specific publishing states
      - You're looking for content information rather than system activity
    </use_case>

    <important_notes>
      1. The org, site, and branch must be provided, ask the user for them if they are not provided.
      2. The org, site, and branch can be derived from the aem page URL. This is of the form: https://${branch}--${site}--${org}.aem.live/${path}
      3. Time filtering parameters (from, to, since) are optional and can be used to limit the logs to specific timeframes.
      4. The 'since' parameter is a relative time (e.g., '1h', '24h', '7d') while 'from' and 'to' are absolute timestamps.
      5. Do not make up any information, only use the information that is provided in the response to answer the user's question.
    </important_notes>

from.description: Start timestamp for filtering logs (ISO 8601 format)

to.description: End timestamp for filtering logs (ISO 8601 format)
